Forecast Discussion

NWS Detroit/Pontiac · 645 PM EDT Fri Oct 23 2026

- The potential exists for dense fog development each of the 
daybreak periods through Monday. Any patchy/dense fog is expected to 
dissipate by around 10 am each morning.

- Mild and dry through the middle of next week.

&&

.AVIATION...

High pressure centered to the east will continue to mark conditions 
this taf period. Attention remains on potential for some degree of 
fog and/or low stratus to develop as low level moisture flux occurs 
with prevailing low level easterly flow off the upstream lakes. The 
overall environment not nearly as favorable as noted last night, 
with the contribution from lake Huron more limited. With that, 
expectation for a response off lake Erie will maintain greater 
potential across portions of the Detroit airspace. Forecast will 
continue to offer a window for LIFR conditions in fog and low 
stratus here. To the north, better setup for MBS given closer 
proximity to Saginaw Bay, while some recent model guidance suggests 
lower likelihood at PTK/FNT. Any lower restriction will 
progressively vacate through late morning, leaving another day of 
mostly clear skies with light winds Saturday.   

D21/DTW Convection... Thunderstorms are not forecast through the TAF 
period.

.DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES...

* Low for cigs/vsby below 200 ft and/or 1/2SM late tonight.
